title: New York's 22nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New York's 22nd Congressional District features first-term Democratic incumbent John Mannion facing Republican challenger Kailee Buller. The district covers Central New York including Syracuse, Utica, Rome, Auburn, and Cortland, with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+4. Mannion flipped the seat in 2024 by defeating Republican incumbent Brandon Williams, while Buller is a former senior U.S. Department of Agriculture official and Auburn native who has positioned herself as a fiscal conservative focused on affordability and agriculture. Political analysts at Cook Political Report rate the race as 'Solid D,' suggesting Mannion holds a strong advantage in this cycle.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found specifically for the NY-22 general election matchup as of mid-June 2026. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D,' and the primary elections were uncontested.

candidates.name: John Mannion
candidates.summary: John Mannion is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 22nd Congressional District, first elected in 2024 after defeating Republican incumbent Brandon Williams. A former high school biology teacher, Mannion previously served in the New York State Senate representing the 50th district from 2020 to 2024. He sits on the House Agriculture Committee and the House Education and Workforce Committee, and is a member of the New Democrat Coalition.

candidates.name: Kailee Buller
candidates.summary: Kailee Buller is the Republican presumptive nominee for New York's 22nd Congressional District. An Auburn native, she served as Chief of Staff to the Deputy Secretary at the U.S. Department of Agriculture under two presidential administrations, where she focused on agricultural policy, food supply chain issues, and regulatory reform. Buller is a graduate of the University at Buffalo and has described herself as a fiscal conservative and moderate Republican focused on lowering costs, energy policy, and supporting working families.

forecast.rationale: No independent public general election polls exist for NY-22 as of mid-June 2026. The forecast relies on structural indicators: a D+4 Cook PVI gives Democrats a modest built-in advantage; first-term Democratic incumbent John Mannion flipped this seat from Republican control in 2024; both primaries were uncontested, suggesting organized party support on each side; and Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D,' indicating analysts see a strong Democratic hold. However, given the absence of any current polling and that Mannion is a freshman incumbent in a district with a history of partisan swings, the appropriate rating is likely_d (80-94% range) rather than safe_d, with medium confidence.
